subject: RE: RFP SLA questions — measurement methodology and credit calc

Subject: RFP: SLA section (uptime, latency, measurement)

Elena,

Thanks — we received the questionnaire. We're drafting a formal response but wanted to flag one quick operational note up front: our platform separates measurement signals into (1) customer-observed metrics at the ingress/load‑balancer layer and (2) service-internal telemetry (server latency, model runtime). For contractual uptime we default to customer-observed measurements but include internal telemetry for root-cause analysis and attribution.

We'll send a consolidated PDF with formulas and examples by Thursday EOD. Sharing to Karthik for the contractual phrasing and to Marcus for the runtime specifics.

- Ava Chen
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: draft SLA wording and credit formula (please review)

Team —

I pulled together a draft response and an example spreadsheet (sla-sampling-calcs.xlsx) that includes three credit scenarios. Key decisions for the RFP:

1) Measurement window: 30-day rolling period aligned with billing month; uptime = (total minutes in month - downtime minutes) / total minutes.
2) Uptime measurement source: primary = customer-observed egress / LB health checks; secondary = server-side telemetry for dispute.
3) Latency SLOs: we propose separate SLOs for first-byte latency and generation-stream latency. Example: first-byte p95 <= 300ms, p99 <= 650ms; streaming token p95 <= 120ms per token for short sequences (<=512 tokens).
4) Sampling: continuous telemetry at 1:1000 sampling of requests for full traces with deterministic aggregation; synthetic probes run every 60s from multiple regions for an independent check.
5) Service credit: linear banding; credit % = min(50%, ((target - observed) / target) * 100 * weight), weighted to prioritize availability over latency. Cap monthly credit at 50% of that month's invoice for Redwood-hosted services.

Neha — can you confirm this aligns with SOC2/contract constraints (especially proof retention)? Marcus — can you confirm p99 measurement points (front-end vs model exec) and whether KV-cache warm start skews short-window p99.

Thanks,
Karthik
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-04T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: draft SLA wording and credit formula (please review)

Karthik — quick checks from compliance:

- Evidence retention: we can provide 12 months of aggregated telemetry and raw logs for the month in question on request (redacted as necessary).
- Sampling artifacts: for disputes we keep sampled full traces and a separate sampling seed log to reconstruct deterministic sampling windows for up to 90 days.
- Maintenance windows: we recommend excluding scheduled maintenance if announced >=72 hours and limited to a 4-hour maintenance window per region per calendar month. We'll need the RFP to accept a scheduled-maintenance exclusion clause.

All good otherwise; I'll add the language around audit rights and log delivery SLA.

-Neha
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: draft SLA wording and credit formula (please review)

Notes on measurement specifics to include in the response:

- Attribution: we attribute region at ingress (LB region tag) and annotate each request with route and model_variant. For multi-region flows we apply a per-request region attribution and compute regional availability independently; global availability rolls up from request weights.
- Measurement point for p95/p99: primary is ingress-to-first-byte observed time (includes network and LB). Model-exec time (kernel/attention runtime) is reported but not used as the contractual p99; we can offer an addendum that binds model-exec tail for Dedicated customers.
- Sampling methodology: deterministic hash sampling on request ID ensures reproducible sample sets; we sample 0.1% of live traffic for full-trace capture and compute percentiles over the sampled population with bias-correction for heavy tails.
- Edge cases: cold-starts, KV-cache warmups, and batch backfills will be excluded from percentile calculations if identified within a 5-minute node-restart window. We'll document the exclusion rules.

I'll attach a short appendix with the pseudo-formulas (included in Redwood_SLA_Response_v1.pdf).

Marcus Lin
Senior Product — Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the questions — please find attached our formal response (Redwood_SLA_Response_v1.pdf) which includes:

1) Contractual uptime calculation and example months showing the math.
2) Latency SLOs separated into first-byte and streaming token latency with p95/p99 targets and worked examples.
3) Measurement methodology: primary customer-observed ingress measurement, deterministic sampling rules, synthetic probe program, and dispute resolution steps.

4) Service credit mechanics with three example computations and the monthly cap at 50% of the invoice.

Quick clarifications: our uplink for contractual uptime uses the ingress LB measurements (this aligns with what your clients observe). Model-runtime telemetry is captured and retained for RCA and can be used in an addendum for Dedicated deployments.
